title: Nightmares after intensive care
stem:
You are an F2 doctor in intensive care. Mrs Ahmed, 55, is recovering after two weeks on a ventilator with pneumonia and is due to move to a ward.

She tells you she has vivid nightmares about being trapped, and has panic attacks when nurses approach her bed at night. She is embarrassed and worried she's "going mad".
instruction: Rank in order the following actions in response to this situation (1 = Most appropriate; 5 = Least appropriate).

options.text: Prescribe a sleeping tablet to help her sleep.
options.brief: Doesn't address the cause and may worsen delirium.
options.detailed: Sedatives can worsen confusion and don't address what she is experiencing.

options.text: Review her for any ongoing delirium or medication effects.
options.detailed: Delirium or medication side effects can contribute. It ranks third because her distress needs addressing first.

options.text: Tell her they're only dreams and will soon pass.
options.detailed: They may pass, but this dismisses how frightening they are.

options.text: Make sure she is referred to the ICU follow-up service or psychological support.
options.brief: Specialist support can help her recover.
options.detailed: Many units offer follow-up after discharge, including psychological support. This helps her recover.

options.text: Listen, and reassure her this is common after intensive care.
options.detailed: Nightmares and anxiety are common after intensive care, often linked to delirium and frightening memories. Knowing this can be a great relief.

explanation.issue: This tests whether you recognise and respond to psychological distress after critical illness.
explanation.keyDetails: She has nightmares and panic attacks. She fears she's going mad. She's moving to a ward.
explanation.reasoning: [E] reassures her, [D] arranges support, and [B] considers physical causes. [A] risks harm, and [C] dismisses her.
explanation.competing: Some would review for delirium first. The key starts with reassurance because she is frightened now, and physical causes can be reviewed alongside.

references.title: Good medical practice
references.note: Domain 2, responding to patients' psychological needs.
